parsed.explanation: Rated as a division under a parent national regime, which sets the floor. The parent regime documents traveller-facing exposure: passport marker restrictions now in effect, with passports confiscated or blocked and some travellers stranded; entry refusal where sex is in doubt; and custody harm in federal and immigration custody. The division adds its own layer. Its governor's order bars trans people from government facilities by birth sex, and a trans visitor was arrested and held 24 hours under trespass enforcement of a bathroom rule. Custody placement follows birth sex, and the only documented trans-prisoner case ended with dismissed claims after a sexual assault. There is no state-wide gender-identity anti-discrimination statute, and the under-19 care ban applies locally. Mitigations are real but partial: national hate-crime and employment/housing enforcement covers gender identity, marriage and adoption are recognised, and sodomy is repealed. Those do not offset the facility and custody exposure, so the division sits below the parent's average.
